title: Air-liquid organotypic assays to investigate cellular crosstalk in the tumor microenvironment of cancer cells
protocol: Pre-coat a 24-well plate with collagen type I at a ratio of 1:100 in PBS.
Add 300 μL of the collagen type I-PBS mixture and incubate for 1 hour at 20°C–22°C.
Wash the wells three times with PBS.
Add 1 mL of DMEM to each well and keep on ice.
Mix 5.25 mL of type I collagen, 1.75 mL of Matrigel, 1 mL of 1× DMEM, 1 mL of 10× DMEM, 1 mL of FBS, and mix on ice using pre-cooled pipette tips until homogenous.
Correct the pH of the gel mixture by adding NaOH drop-by-drop while mixing gently with pre-cooled pipette tips.
Assess the pH based on phenol red color change.
Remove DMEM from the pre-coated 24-well plate.
Add 1 mL of gel mix using pre-cooled tips.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour to allow gel polymerization.
Gently add 1 mL of 1× DMEM to equilibrate the gels.
Incubate at 37°C for 18-24 hours.
Prepare cancer/stromal cells and membrane.
Detach the cells using pre-warmed reagents.
Aspirate DMEM from the cells.
Wash once with 5 mL of PBS.
Add 2 mL of 0.25% trypsin and incubate for 5 minutes at 37°C.
Neutralize the trypsin with 2 mL of DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 250 g at 20°C–22°C.
Resuspend in 2 mL of DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS.
Count cancer and stromal cells.
Prepare aliquots containing 1 × 10^6 cells/mL in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS.
Mix the cells in a 1:1 proportion by adding 500 μL of each cell type (cancer and stromal).
Seed the cells onto the equilibrated organotypic gel using a p1000 micropipette to avoid disruption of the gel.
Add 1 mL of cancer/stromal cell mix on top of the gel.
Let the cells embed into the gel overnight in the incubator.
Prepare collagen type I gel mix (2.5 mL).
Gently mix 1,750 μL of type I collagen with 250 μL of 1× DMEM, 250 μL of 10× DMEM, and 250 μL of FBS on ice using pre-cooled tips.
Pipette up and down several times with pre-cooled tips until the gel mix becomes homogenous.
Keep the mixture on ice.
Correct gel pH by adding 1 N NaOH drop-by-drop until the gel mix turns pink.
Gently pipette up and down with pre-cooled tips to ensure uniform color throughout the gel mix.
Place autoclaved membranes in a sterile cell culture plate, one membrane per gel.
Add 250 μL of collagen type I mixture per membrane using pre-cooled tips.
Incubate the membranes with the collagen type I mixture for 15 minutes at 37°C.
Add 10 mL of ice-cold 1% glutaraldehyde in PBS solution to the plate containing the membranes.
Incubate the membranes for 1 h at 4°C.
Discard the membranes that detach from the plate.
Aspirate the 1% glutaraldehyde in PBS solution.
Wash the membranes four times with 5 mL of PBS.
Add 10 mL of 1× DMEM to the plates.
Seal the plates with parafilm.
Incubate the plates overnight (18 h) at 4°C.
Place the 2.5 cm² stainless steel grid in a 6-well plate.
Place the 2.5 cm² pre-coated 100 μm nylon membrane on top of the grid.
Place the organotypic gel containing the cells on the nylon membrane.
Remove DMEM from the organotypic gels using a p1000 micropipette to avoid gel disruption.
Carefully take the gel using two sterilized spatulas.
Place the gel on top of the grid + membrane structure.
Add approximately 6-7 mL of DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS to cover the structure and avoid touching the gel.
Add media from the vertex of the grid to prevent bubble formation below the mesh.
Replace the media every 2-3 days.
Fix the membrane after 15 days.
Label a 6-well plate with 2 mL of 10% Neutral buffered formalin (NBF).
Using forceps, pick up the membrane and collapsed gel carefully from the vertex.
Transfer the membrane with the gel into the NBF.
Let the membrane fix for 2 hours at 20°C-22°C without movement.
Transfer the membrane from the NBF to a new 6-well plate containing 70% ethanol.
Paraffin embed the membrane.
Cut the membrane into three pieces using a scalpel or scissors.
Place each piece in a tissue cassette perpendicular to the sponge.
Keep the cut membranes in 70% ethanol until paraffin embedding is performed.
Embed samples in paraffin, placing the membrane as shown in Figure 5B.
Cut the paraffin blocks and prepare sections for staining.
Stain the sections using standard protocols such as hematoxylin and eosin (H&E).
